files.content:
# paste-guard

Strip emails, card numbers, phone numbers, IPs and API keys out of text before you paste it into an AI tool — review every replacement first, then put the real values back into the answer locally.

## The problem

People paste support tickets, logs and customer emails into AI assistants every day to get a summary or a draft reply. Those texts are full of customer emails, phone numbers, card numbers and the occasional API key. Company policy says "don't paste personal data", but nobody has a quick, reliable way to clean a ticket in the 30 seconds they have.

## Who it's for

Support agents, operations staff and developers who use AI tools at work with real tickets and logs — and the team leads who need them to do it safely.

## What it does

- Detects emails, Luhn-valid card numbers, phone numbers, IPv4 addresses and common secret formats (`sk-…`, `ghp_…`, `AKIA…`, `xox…-`, private key headers).
- Replaces each value with a stable placeholder: the same email becomes `[EMAIL_1]` everywhere, so the AI's answer still makes sense.
- **Review first:** by default it only prints a table of what it would replace (originals masked). Nothing is written until you re-run with `--approve`.
- Never overwrites a file: `--out` and `--map` must be new file names.
- `restore` puts the real values back into the AI's reply using the local mapping file.

## Try it

Requires Node 18+. No install step, no dependencies. All example data is invented.

```bash
node cli.js redact examples/ticket.txt
node cli.js redact examples/ticket.txt --approve --out safe.txt --map map.json
node cli.js restore reply.txt --map map.json
node --test
```

Step 1 prints a review table of 6 replacements and writes nothing. Step 2 writes `safe.txt` (paste this into the AI tool) and `map.json` (keep this local). Step 3 prints the AI's reply with the real values restored.

## Acceptance criteria

- Emails, Luhn-valid cards, phones, IPs and listed key formats are replaced; order ids, totals, dates and Luhn-invalid numbers are left alone.
- The same value always maps to the same placeholder.
- Without `--approve`, no file is written; with it, existing files are never overwritten.
- The review table never shows an original value in full.
- `restore` replaces known placeholders and leaves unknown ones untouched.

## How it's built

`src/redact.js` runs an ordered list of regex detectors per line (secrets and emails first, the loose phone pattern last), with extra checks where patterns alone over-match: a Luhn checksum for cards and a digit-count and date check for phones. `cli.js` handles the review-then-approve flow and the no-overwrite rule.

## Limits and safety

- **Pattern-based detection misses things**: names, addresses, account numbers and free-text personal details are not detected. The review step is there because a person must still read the text before sharing it.
- `map.json` contains the real values. Keep it on your machine and delete it when you're done.
- This reduces risk; it does not make a text safe to share by itself, and it doesn't replace your company's data policy.

## Contribute

- Add IBAN detection with checksum validation.
- Add a `--types EMAIL,CARD` option to choose which detectors run.
- Read from the clipboard and write back to it, for a one-command flow.

---

Scaffolded by an automated weekly pipeline, then refined by hand — see the factory repo for how it works.

Support ticket #4821 (all details below are invented for this example)

Customer jane.doe@example.com says checkout fails after entering card 4242 4242 4242 4242.
She called from +44 20 7946 0958 on 2026-10-14 at 14:05.
Our logs show the request came from 203.0.113.42 and the payment service used key sk-EXAMPLEONLY-not-a-real-key-0000.
Escalated to billing; jane.doe@example.com was told we'd reply within 24 hours.
Order total 129.99, order id 100045.

issue.title: Add a --types option to choose detectors
issue.body:
Good first issue! Sometimes you want to keep IP addresses (e.g. when asking an AI about a network problem). Add `--types EMAIL,CARD,PHONE,IP,SECRET` so only the listed detector types run.

- In `src/redact.js`, let `redact(text, { types })` skip detectors whose `type` isn't listed (default: all).
- Pass the option through from `cli.js`.
- Add one test in `test/redact.test.js`.

Should take well under an hour — comment here to claim it.
